title: Process Crash Restart Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Process Crash Restart Record within the Runtime Failure and Recovery Records Database. Supports diagnosis of crashes, failed processes, and service interruptions. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record reconstructs the failure timeline first: what failed, in what order, and what the system did next. Recovery is then described as ordered steps with a check after each one, so a responder can tell whether recovery is working or stalling. Downtime and recovery time are computed from the timeline, not estimated from memory.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: minute 0 - failure detected. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

An operator uses these records during an incident and after it: during, as a checklist; after, as the factual basis for the review that prevents a repeat. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Process Crash Restart Record: rebuild the incident timeline and compute recovery time.
events = [('failure detected', 0), ('diagnosis complete', 8), ('recovery started', 12), ('service restored', 26), ('verified healthy', 31)]
start = events[0][1]
for name, minute in events:
    print("minute", minute, "-", name)
downtime = events[3][1] - start
print("downtime minutes:", downtime)
print("time to verified healthy minutes:", events[4][1] - start)
print("recovery steps recorded:", len(events))

minute 0 - failure detected
minute 8 - diagnosis complete
minute 12 - recovery started
minute 26 - service restored
minute 31 - verified healthy
downtime minutes: 26
time to verified healthy minutes: 31
recovery steps recorded: 5
